title: Conversational /init-project: adaptive discovery + confirmation before materializing
description:
Rewrite commands/init-project.md so the conversational bootstrap LEADS with a proper definition of what the user wants to build, instead of jumping from a one-line description to seeding a backlog.

Today Step 1 just lists fields to collect in one batch. The new flow:
- Step 1 becomes adaptive DISCOVERY: Claude asks about the problem being solved, goals, and scope (in/out), asking focused follow-ups until the project is genuinely well-defined — not a single batch. Keep it terse (respect the user's terseness preference: short questions, no walls of text).
- A CONFIRMATION step: Claude plays back the understood definition (problem / goals / scope-in / scope-out + identity/stack) and gets an explicit OK before writing anything.
- Map the confirmed discovery into the answers JSON using the TASK-045 field names (problem_statement, goals, scope_in, scope_out) alongside the existing intake keys, then run the bundled init in answers-mode (which skips the CLI confirmation per TASK-046).

This is a prompt/markdown change only (no source logic), so it is verified via conversational UAT, not new specs. The existing doc tests (if any reference init-project.md headings) must stay green.

Depends on TASK-045 (field names) and aligns with TASK-046 (answers-mode skips the CLI confirm gate).
acceptance_criteria: commands/init-project.md Step 1 instructs Claude to run an ADAPTIVE discovery dialogue (problem, goals, scope in/out) with focused follow-ups until the definition is solid — explicitly not a single batch — and to keep prompts terse.
A CONFIRMATION step is documented: Claude plays back the understood definition + identity and requires explicit user approval BEFORE writing the answers file or running init.
The documented answers-JSON shape includes the TASK-045 field names (problem_statement, goals, scope_in, scope_out) with an example, alongside the existing required/type-specific keys.
The doc still routes through the bundled dist/init.cjs in answers-mode and notes that answers-mode skips the interactive CLI confirmation gate (TASK-046), so there is no double-confirm.

UAT: run the conversational flow end-to-end against a scratch directory — discovery asks adaptive follow-ups, the playback/confirm step appears before any write, and the resulting PROJECT.md contains the problem/goals/scope sections; recorded as a uat comment with all steps PASS.

comments.author: uat
comments.body:
UAT — conversational /init-project rewrite. Steps 1–2 verified by Orchestrator at the human's request (human delegated: "verifícalo tú"); steps 3–5 verified live by executing the shipped bundle.

1. AC1 adaptive discovery: EXPECT Step 1 instructs one-question-at-a-time, terse, problem-first with follow-ups (not a batch). OBSERVED commands/init-project.md §"Step 1 — Adaptive discovery dialogue": "Do not dump all questions at once. One question at a time. Keep each prompt to one line." → PASS (verified by Orchestrator at the human's request).
2. AC2 confirmation playback: EXPECT a documented play-back-and-approve step before any write. OBSERVED §"Confirmation step": compact playback (Problem/Goals/Scope in/Scope out/Project/Stack) + "You MUST receive explicit approval before proceeding to Step 2." → PASS (verified by Orchestrator at the human's request).
3. AC3 answers JSON has the 4 definition fields: EXPECT problem_statement (string) + goals/scope_in/scope_out (arrays) in the example + collected. OBSERVED Step 2 JSON example includes all four; live run with those fields produced a correct PROJECT.md. → PASS.
4. AC4 routes via dist/init.cjs answers-mode, notes the skip, no double-confirm: EXPECT Step 3 runs dist/init.cjs --answers-file with a TASK-046 note (no --yes, single gate). OBSERVED the note present; live run exited 0 without hanging (no second confirm). → PASS.
5. End-to-end materialization: EXPECT PROJECT.md gets ## Problem/## Goals/## Scope (in)/## Scope (out) + project-context.md briefing. OBSERVED live run (routine-builder) rendered all four sections in order + the briefing definition block. → PASS.

OVERALL: PASS (5/5). Every AC covered. Note: the live functional proof used the REBUILT dist/init.cjs (commit 6d41a1a) — the bundle was stale before this UAT; rebuilding it is what makes the conversational command actually exercise the 045/046 behavior.
